title: Rates of Reaction Adventure 2 · Calculations
welcome_lead: Time to calculate rates and read them off graphs. Units matter!
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry rate calculations — mean rate, gradient from graph, units cm³/s g/s.
final_note: You can now compute mean rates and recognise units in any rates problem.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mean rate = quantity changed ÷ time taken.

If 48 cm³ of gas is made in 24 seconds, mean rate = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm³/s.

Always include the units. cm³/s for gas, g/s for mass loss, mol/dm³ per second for concentration.

On a graph of product against time, the gradient (slope) is the rate.

Steep line = fast rate. Flat line = reaction has stopped.

Gradient = rise ÷ run = change in y ÷ change in x. For a straight section, pick two points and divide.

For a curve, the rate changes. To find the rate at one moment, draw a tangent — a straight line that just touches the curve at that point.

Then measure the tangent's gradient (rise ÷ run).

Rates are usually highest at the start, when concentrations are highest, and fall as reactants run out.

The rate of reaction

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.

numericals.q: A reaction loses 12 g of mass in 4 minutes. What is the mean rate in g/s? (Convert minutes to seconds first.)
numericals.hint: 4 minutes = 240 seconds. Then rate = mass ÷ time in seconds.
